title: Implement weight profiler and atomic shard activation to reduce model ingest tail latency
creator: Nora Patel
description:
Problem: In the current model ingest path we observe long tail latency during large weight bundle uploads and shard initialization. Root causes identified in prior investigations: (1) synchronous per-shard metadata verification that blocks bootstrap, (2) repeated weight format autodetection passes over compressed archives, and (3) tokenizer schema handshakes being performed inline with checkpoint memory mapping. These contribute to unrecoverable spikes when loading >8GB model artifacts or when many small shards are registered concurrently.

Goal: Reduce worst-case model load latency and lower CPU/IO contention during ingest by introducing: (A) a lightweight Weight Profiler component to do a single-pass, low-cost sampling that emits an index of shard formats and sizes; (B) an atomic shard activation protocol that separates verification from activation and enables parallel prefetching and staged mapping; and (C) an asynchronous tokenizer registration step with compatibility checks that do not block activation.

Proposed approach:
- Weight Profiler: implement a streaming sampler that reads the minimum prefixes from archive blobs to classify format (e.g., .pt sharded, safetensors, legacy tarball) and approximate compressed size. Profiler will produce a small manifest used by downstream loaders. Profiling must be IO-efficient and avoid full decompression.
- Atomic Shard Activation: change the runtime shard lifecycle to two phases: VERIFY -> STAGED -> ACTIVATED. VERIFY performs fast manifest checks and checksum sampling; STAGED prefetches key pages and reserves memory; ACTIVATED switches routing to the shard. The transition STAGED->ACTIVATED must be atomic from router point-of-view to avoid serving incomplete shards.
- Tokenizer decoupling: move tokenizer format detection and validation to a background task triggered by VERIFY. If tokenizer compatibility is uncertain, activate a safe compatibility shim (vocab adapter) and enqueue a tokenizer reconciliation job.

Backward compatibility and rollout: default to existing behavior unless cluster flag "ingest_atomic_activation" is enabled. Implement feature gate and a canary rollout tied to model size and customer tier. Provide fast fallback: if STAGED step fails, revert to legacy single-threaded load.

Success criteria / metrics:
- 95th percentile model load time reduced by 40% for artifacts >4GB in staging tests.
- Peak CPU IO wait during parallel ingests reduced by 30%.
- No increase in failed activations in production beyond historical 0.2%.

Testing plan:
- Unit tests for profiler format heuristics and false-positive/negative rates.
- Integration tests: parallel ingest harness with synthetic shards (mixed formats) to validate atomic activation semantics and router atomicity.
- Canary: enable flag for small subset of Dedicated and Hosted infra, monitor model-load latency, activation failures, and downstream inference error rates.

Risks and trade-offs:
- Profiler misclassification could cause wrong prefetch strategy; mitigate with conservative defaults and fallback to full scan on mismatch.
- STAGED reserving memory could increase peak memory usage; implement reservation caps and eviction heuristics.
- Tokenizer shim may impact early inference quality; ensure graceful degradation and trigger reconciliation ASAP.

Docs and artifacts: implementation design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/Weight+Profiler+and+Atomic+Activation, prototype PR with benchmarks: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/5642, ingest harness dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/ingest-harness/model-load-canary
